summary: HTTP request telemetry is missing; a business event metric is optional and not approved.

evidence.finding: Go chi service without OpenTelemetry dependencies

signal_flow.component_flow_map:
Request handling
main.go [SOURCE-COVERED] -> chi router [GAP: HTTP request telemetry] -> POST /tasks handler [SOURCE-COVERED] [GAP: Task creation KPI] [GAP: Task telemetry ownership] [GAP: Task creation trace]

findings.title: HTTP requests lack route-aware telemetry
findings.gap: The chi router has no OpenTelemetry server instrumentation.
findings.impact: Operators cannot attribute latency or errors to stable route patterns.
findings.product_outcome: Splunk APM route-level latency and errors
findings.required_fix: Add one OpenTelemetry SDK lifecycle and one route-aware otelhttp server wrapper.
acceptance_criteria: GET /health emits exactly one HTTP server span with http.route=/health.
constraints: Preserve the existing chi routes and startup command.

expected_telemetry.name: GET /health
expected_telemetry.product_view: Splunk APM route-level latency and errors

follow_up_actions: Verify the route span in the local runtime and APM trace view.

findings.title: Task creation has no business counter
findings.gap: Successful task creation is not counted as a business event.
findings.impact: Product activity cannot be charted independently of HTTP throughput.
findings.required_fix: Add a task.created counter after a task is persisted.
acceptance_criteria: A successful task creation increments task.created exactly once.
constraints: Keep the metric free of task, user, title, and other unbounded dimensions.
follow_up_actions: Create a KPI chart only if the product owner approves this finding.

findings.title: Choose one task-creation telemetry owner
findings.gap: The service does not define whether task creation should emit the task.created metric or the task.create span.
findings.impact: Implementing both alternatives would duplicate the same task-creation outcome in two app-owned signals.
findings.product_outcome: Task creation has one explicitly chosen app-owned telemetry signal.
findings.required_fix: Choose either the task.created metric or the task.create span as the app-owned task-creation signal.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one of task.created or task.create is implemented and proven.
constraints: Do not emit both app-owned alternatives for the same task creation.
follow_up_actions: Record the chosen signal owner before selecting the compatible instrumentation branch.
findings.decision_question: Which app-owned OTel signal should represent task creation: task.created or task.create?

decision_options.label: Task metric
decision_options.outcome: Emit task.created once after successful persistence.

findings.title: Trace successful task creation
findings.gap: Successful task creation has no app-owned task.create span.
findings.impact: When the span alternative is chosen, operators cannot isolate persistence latency in the trace waterfall.
findings.product_outcome: The trace waterfall shows one bounded task.create span for each successful creation.
findings.required_fix: Add one task.create span around successful task persistence.
acceptance_criteria: A successful task creation emits task.create exactly once.
constraints: Do not attach task IDs, titles, users, or other unbounded values.
follow_up_actions: Inspect the task.create trace waterfall only when the trace-span option is selected.

scenarios.acceptance_criteria: The request emits exactly one server span with http.route=/health.

scenarios.trigger: POST /tasks with a valid bounded title
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: The successful persistence path records task.created exactly once with no metric attributes.

scenarios.trigger: POST /tasks with a valid bounded title
scenarios.acceptance_criteria: The successful persistence path emits task.create exactly once.

recommendation: Review findings in order, save a selected audit copy as .observe/otel-audit.selected.json, then run $otel-instrument.
